population.note: FICTIONAL. Reconciliation, with ever-users at 17% of adults: ~65% of them have stopped at least once (11.1 pp). ~40% of stoppers restarted (4.4 pp, or 26% of ever-users). Never-stopped users are 17 − 11.1 = 5.9 pp, which is 35% of ever-users and matches the starting one-year persistence of 34–36%. So current users = 5.9 + 4.4 ≈ 10.2 pp, and off now = 11.1 − 4.4 = 6.7 ≈ 17 − 10.2 = 6.8 pp. The off-drug population (≈17.7M adults) is now larger than the never-stopped one (≈15.3M). It skews to the middle and bottom thirds and to people 65+ who lost Bridge coverage. Age bands, weighted by adult population shares (~20/33/25/22%), give ≈10.2. Current users ≈26.5M (10.2% of ~260M adults). Who pays: employer plans ~8.5M; Medicare (diabetes/CVD/OSA/CKD codes) ~4.0M; Medicaid ~2.5M; legal cash pay (authorised generic, direct-to-consumer orals, brand self-pay) ~8.0M; gray market ~3.5M, of whom ~0.4M are on unapproved or pre-approval retatrutide. Surveys probably undercount gray-market users by an unknown margin. Under-18: ~0.3% of all children (~220k), up from ~0.1% in 2026. Still mostly 12+. Upper-income skew persists, though narrowed by the $69 authorised generic. Overall adoption fell 0.8 pp despite the price collapse. Three things drove it: the Medicare Bridge pilot expiring (Dec 2027), employer retreat, and adherence-conditioned coverage ending coverage for non-adherent members. Cheap cash access partly refilled the gap but did not close it.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot expired 31 Dec 2027 as scheduled. At its 2027 peak it covered ~1.4M beneficiaries for obesity: 1.4M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.1B/yr in federal spend, consistent with the CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–34 had it continued. It was not renewed. CMS guidance from Jan 2028 restricts Part D coverage to labelled cardiometabolic indications (type 2 diabetes, established CVD, OSA, CKD, MASH). About 0.6M Bridge enrollees qualified on those codes; ~0.8M lost coverage. Medicaid: ~16 states cover obesity at the federal reference price. At least nine condition continued coverage on ≥80% refill adherence (proportion of days covered) and ≥5% weight loss at 16 weeks, verified through pharmacy claims and, in four states, a connected-pen data feed.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ brands at $6–40/month, exported to ~100 countries. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 60–95/month and the main source for US cross-border personal importation. Brazil, Mexico, Türkiye: local generics. Cost-plus generic injectable now available in ~170 countries. Generic tirzepatide has not launched anywhere major.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Novo Nordisk launched an authorised generic semaglutide injection (Oct 2027) through a wholly owned subsidiary at $69/month, all doses. It is sold through retail pharmacies and TrumpRx. This is the only US 'generic' semaglutide; no ANDA generic is approved. Generic liraglutide fell to $45–60/month. Lilly answered with Foundayo cash at $99 (all doses) and Zepbound vials at $299–449. Newly approved retatrutide lists at $1,299 cash and is covered by few plans. List Wegovy $1,349 is unchanged and almost nobody pays it. Below-$75 access makes this an income-floor question: $69 is $828/year, and that is the gap for the bottom third. Employer coverage for weight management fell 60% → 42% (2028 survey). Remaining coverage is concentrated on diabetes and cardiac codes, often with BMI-surcharge wellness programmes attached. The gray market regrew in three channels: 'research-use-only' peptide vendors (retatrutide, cagrilintide, and since 2028 'myostatin-pathway' antibodies of unknown identity), Indian and Canadian personal-import mail order, and 503A compounders relabelling as 'personalised'. FDA's 503B exclusion was finalised in 2027 but does not reach these channels.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; authorised generic semaglutide from Oct 2027)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Dec 2026)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2028)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of incident dementia in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide injection, May 2028; contested)
adjunct to smoking/vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (Wegovy pill, Jul 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: sNDA for alcohol use disorder with obesity under review; widely prescribed off-label
microdosing for 'metabolic health' and 'food noise' in people without obesity, largely through the gray market and the $69 authorised generic
cognitive 'protection' in middle-aged people without diabetes, extrapolated from the dementia label; unsupported by its evidence
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling, compulsive shopping and cannabis craving: observational and anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. CagriSema was approved Dec 2026, from review already under way at the start, and sells modestly after losing to tirzepatide on efficacy. Retatrutide: BLA filed Feb 2027, approved Mar 2028 (≥12 months after filing), label carrying dysesthesia and the class anhedonia language; ~28% mean loss. Muscle-preserving combination: the drawn launch is not allowed on the US market by end-2028 under approval rules, so it is realised as a filing. Lilly reported phase 3 of bimagrumab + tirzepatide (Q1 2028): lean mass fell from ~33% of weight lost to ~9%, with similar total loss. It filed a BLA in Jun 2028 with a National Priority Voucher and expects a decision in 2029. Marketing, analyst notes and the fitness industry already treat the 'skinny-frail' problem as solved, and gray-market 'muscle-sparing stacks' sell on that claim now. Amycretin: phase 3 ongoing, filing expected 2029; not on market. Survodutide: filed Q3 2027, decision expected late 2028 or 2029. MariTide (monthly): phase 3, not on market.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect and still the leading cause of discontinuation. Higher at retatrutide top doses. Gray-market users report more severe escalation episodes because they titrate by themselves.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more cases with 28% loss on retatrutide.
Long-term RCT and CVOT data still show no confirmed causal link; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; multidistrict litigation ongoing, no verdicts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–35% of weight lost is lean mass on current monotherapies. The bimagrumab combination phase 3 cut this to ~9%, but the combination is not approved. Bone-density and fracture signals in adults 65+ are being studied.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on monotherapy labels. FDA reviewing the combination BLA; industry messaging already treats the problem as solved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Further cohorts conflict; pooled estimate of a small elevated relative risk with wide confidence intervals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' labelling for semaglutide; FDA added it to post-marketing adverse reactions (2027) without a class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in further reviews. Kept separate from the anhedonia finding, which regulators distinguish explicitly.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA pooled analysis (2027) of trials that added the SHAPS anhedonia scale and post-marketing studies: clinically meaningful reduced pleasure or emotional blunting in ~1.8% on drug vs ~0.8% placebo, an excess of about 1 in 100. Dose-related; ~2.5% at retatrutide top doses. Most cases resolve within 8 weeks of dose reduction or stopping. Uncommon, but at ~26.5M users that is roughly a quarter-million excess cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling, Jun 2027: Adverse Reactions plus a Patient Information line, 'reduced interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy'. Clinics screen with a two-item question at dose escalation. Manufacturers market the same mechanism for smoking and alcohol indications.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Larger real-world datasets confirm substantial regain for most people. Roughly half to two-thirds of lost weight returns within a year, varying by dose and duration. Smaller real-world regain figures turned out to reflect selection.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on labels. Used by payers to justify adherence-conditioned coverage and by manufacturers to justify chronic use.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More observational data on iron, B12, vitamin D and protein shortfall at large calorie deficits.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Clinical society guidance (2027) recommends baseline and annual labs; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of RCT follow-up now exists; still no adolescent data beyond ~4 years. Cycling cohorts show greater fat regain than lean regain per cycle, a 'body-composition ratchet' that has not been confirmed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Post-marketing requirements on retatrutide and CagriSema; an NIH cycling cohort was funded in 2028.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / research-peptide product harms (dosing errors, contamination, misidentified molecules)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product exceed 4,000 cumulative. Independent assays find a minority of 'research' retatrutide vials mislabelled or underdosed. Several hospitalisations involve unidentified 'myostatin' injectables.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised (2027); import alerts on Indian finished-dose shipments; warning letters continue. Enforcement is outpaced by offshore and Telegram-based vendors.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysesthesia (abnormal skin sensation) with triple agonists
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in retatrutide phase 3 and confirmed in early post-approval use; mostly mild and transient.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure continues in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks. Unit declines are low single-digit annually in those categories and flat to slightly down overall. 'GLP-1-friendly' labelling is so common it means nothing; protein and fibre callouts are standard. Mid-size snack makers consolidate. Big CPG offsets volume with price-per-gram increases on small packs. The cheap authorised generic widens the affected household base into lower-income shoppers.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes contracting faster than pre-2026 trend. The smoking-cessation label and widespread off-label alcohol use make reduced drinking clinically endorsed. Diageo and Brown-Forman cut US guidance again. Premium low-volume 'occasion' pours and non-alcoholic lines grow but do not replace lost heavy-drinker revenue.

restaurants.state: Traffic roughly holds. Check composition shifts to smaller plates, shared formats and fewer second drinks. Casual-dining chains with heavy appetiser and dessert mixes underperform. Fast-casual protein bowls outperform. All-you-can-eat buffets close at an accelerating local rate.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists still contracting: store closures and one Chapter 11 restructuring among regional chains. Mainstream apparel's re-buying wave is fading. Alterations and resale benefit. Sizing ranges at mass retailers shrink at the top end, a visible signal to people who are off the drug.

fitness.state: Strength training and 'muscle-preservation' programmes grow. Gyms sell DEXA scans and on-drug coaching. Expected approval of the muscle-sparing combination is already reshaping marketing toward 'look, not lean mass'. Some coaches warn that the narrative will reduce the urgency of training.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage down to 42%. Remaining coverage runs through cardiometabolic codes, prior authorisation and adherence verification. Health-contingent wellness programmes with BMI surcharges have spread. Pharmacy trend has moderated as semaglutide unit costs collapse, and some carriers cite the $69 authorised generic as the reason to stop covering obesity at all.

pharma.state: Revenue mix shifting. Semaglutide revenue per patient has collapsed in the US and ex-US. Novo Nordisk restructures and uses the authorised generic to hold share against gray imports. Lilly grows on tirzepatide, Foundayo volume and retatrutide. Global incretin revenue grows more slowly than 2026 forecasts as price erosion offsets volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among middle-aged professionals, a lean body is unremarkable and assumed to be medicated. A body that has regained weight is read as a lapse in coverage, money or adherence: 'are you off it?' is a normal, faintly intrusive question. Normalisation is strongest among women 40–64 in suburban professional communities, for example the north Dallas suburbs of Plano and Frisco, where staying on is treated like dental care.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The price gap has narrowed: $69 cash makes the drug reachable for much of the middle third. Class now shows in which molecule people take (retatrutide and Zepbound vs authorised generic semaglutide), in whether they are monitored (employer and Medicaid adherence programmes vs private cash), and in who has dropped off. The bottom third and older adults who lost Bridge coverage make up most of the off-drug population.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Small plates, shared mains and protein-first ordering are the default at middle-class dinners. Holiday and wedding meals are the main remaining sites of large-portion eating. Some users schedule 'skip weeks' around them, and gray-market users do this more. Many hosts now ask guests about appetite the way they once asked about allergies.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating app profiles routinely list 'on it / off it / never'. The anhedonia label gave couples vocabulary, and 'is it the drug or is it us?' is a recognised therapy-room question. Some couples counsellors ask about dose changes at intake.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of all kinds is treated clinically. With smoking and dementia indications, the drug is described less as a diet aid and more as a general-purpose 'metabolic and brain' medicine. That framing makes stopping look like neglect rather than choice.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Labelled since Jun 2027 at ~1.8% vs ~0.8% placebo (an excess of about 1 in 100), dose-related and mostly reversible. Clinicians treat it as uncommon and manageable by dose reduction. Because ~26.5M adults are on drug, the absolute number is large enough that most people know someone who has 'dialled down to feel things again'.
interior_life.framing: An uncommon, labelled side effect, managed like sexual dysfunction on SSRIs. The same mechanism is marketed as treatment in the smoking-cessation label and the pending alcohol filing. Clinicians describe it as 'the same dial, turned too far for some'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: No measured productivity effect. Some employers' wellness vendors include the two-item anhedonia screen in check-ins, and a few employees report hiding symptoms to avoid having their dose reduced and missing weight targets tied to premium discounts. Sales and hospitality workers are the most vocal about blunted social energy.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians, comedians and chefs are the visible subgroup openly discussing dose-cutting before tours, openings or tasting menus. Some deliberately cycle off for creative periods, accepting regain. Sour, spicy and very bitter flavours stay popular among users as 'something you can still feel'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is acknowledged on labels as part of the anhedonia language. Couples report renegotiating, with dose timing around anniversaries and holidays. Not a mass phenomenon, but routine in clinic conversations.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Limited. The anhedonia label became a talking point for food-freedom and anti-pharma commentators. Medicaid adherence monitoring drew bipartisan privacy criticism in two state legislatures. No measurable effect on turnout or partisanship.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-speed on approvals: retatrutide approved on schedule, the combination filed with a priority voucher, the dementia indication approved despite a split advisory committee. Pro-price through the authorised-generic arrangement, welcomed by the administration as a TrumpRx win. Enforcement-heavy against compounders but unable to contain offshore research-peptide and personal-import channels.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The Medicare Bridge pilot was allowed to expire (Dec 2027), leaving coverage to cardiometabolic codes. Medicaid obesity coverage in ~16 states at the federal reference price, increasingly set against the $69 cash benchmark. TrumpRx carries the authorised generic.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits are conditioned on adherence and BMI. At least nine state Medicaid programmes end obesity coverage after missed refills (<80% proportion of days covered) or <5% loss at 16 weeks; four use connected-pen dose logs. Employers use health-contingent wellness rules under the existing HIPAA/ACA framework, which allows premium variance of up to 30%. A BMI-based surcharge is waived through the required 'reasonable alternative standard', which is increasingly defined as verified GLP-1 adherence. Gray-market purchasing is partly a response: some users buy off-books so no adherence or BMI record exists.
state.workforce_or_military: DoD keeps TRICARE weight-only exclusions. Recruiting commands accept applicants who have been off the drug ≥90 days with stable weight, prompting reports of recruits stopping to enlist. Some long-haul trucking and airline medical examiners require disclosure of GLP-1 use, but none bar it.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India is the world's cost-plus supplier and a source of US gray imports. FDA import alerts target Indian finished-dose shipments, and Canadian cross-border pharmacies fill the gap. The authorised generic is partly a commercial response to that leakage. Retatrutide and next-gen peptides for the gray market come mainly from Chinese peptide synthesisers.

events.event: FDA adds 'reduced interest or pleasure / emotional blunting' to all incretin obesity labels after a pooled analysis finds ~1.8% vs 0.8% on placebo, dose-related and largely reversible
Novo Nordisk launches an authorised generic semaglutide injection at $69/month through retail pharmacies and TrumpRx; Lilly cuts Foundayo cash to $99

Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot expires unrenewed; CMS limits Part D coverage to diabetes, cardiac, sleep apnea, kidney and liver codes; ~0.8M beneficiaries lose obesity coverage. Employer weight-loss coverage falls to 42% in the 2028 survey
Nine state Medicaid programmes begin ending GLP-1 obesity coverage for members below 80% refill adherence or 5% weight loss at 16 weeks; four require connected-pen dose logs
FDA approves retatrutide at $1,299/month list; an estimated 400,000 Americans were already injecting gray-market 'research' retatrutide, and vendors cut prices to ~$120 a vial

FDA approves semaglutide for dementia risk reduction in type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular disease after a 7–6 advisory vote; weeks later Wegovy pill gains a smoking-cessation indication and Lilly files its muscle-sparing bimagrumab–tirzepatide combination

open_tensions: Price is solved but not access: at $69 the drug is cheap, yet the people off it are disproportionately the bottom third and older adults who lost Bridge coverage. Whoever still pays now attaches monitoring, so privacy is becoming the new access barrier.

Adherence-conditioned benefits push some users into the gray market to avoid records. That market now carries unapproved next-gen molecules and unidentified 'muscle-sparing' injectables ahead of the combination's 2029 decision.

Anhedonia is labelled as a 1-in-100 harm while the same mechanism is marketed as therapy for nicotine and pending for alcohol. Wellness programmes screen for it and also tie premium discounts to staying on the drug.

The dementia label rests on contested evidence and is fuelling prevention-minded use among people without diabetes. The mass of cycling users means the body-composition and long-horizon effects of on/off use are still unmeasured.
still_true: No ANDA (independent) generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is FDA-approved; compound exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32 (the only US generic is Novo's own authorised generic).
Wegovy list price remains $1,349/month and almost nobody pays it.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels in Jan 2026 stays removed.
TrumpRx remains the federal cash-pay channel for Lilly and Novo products.
Foundayo (orforglipron) and the Wegovy pill remain on the US market, and the route mix is still split between weekly injectables and daily orals.

prose.headline: $69 a Month and a Pen That Reports Back: Thin Got Cheap in 2028. Staying Covered Means Being Watched
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 the drug is cheap and the question has changed. Since October 2027 a pharmacy counter in any American town will sell a month of semaglutide for sixty-nine dollars. It is Novo Nordisk's own authorised generic, launched to stem the flow of Indian and Canadian vials through the mail. Lilly answered with its daily pill at ninety-nine. The price argument that ran through 2026 has stopped, but not because everyone is on it. Slightly fewer American adults take an incretin now than two years ago, about one in ten, and the people who stopped now outnumber the people who never have.

The arithmetic is unglamorous. The Medicare Bridge pilot ended on schedule at the close of 2027, and roughly eight hundred thousand older adults found their obesity coverage gone unless they carried a diabetes or cardiac code. Employers kept retreating; fewer than half now cover weight management at all, and some cite the sixty-nine-dollar price as the reason. For a household that never had eight hundred dollars a year to spare, cheap is not cheap enough. And where someone still pays, they want proof. Nine state Medicaid programmes cut members off below eighty percent refill adherence or five percent weight loss by week sixteen. Four of them read dose logs straight from connected pens. Employers do the same through wellness rules written in the last decade. There is a BMI surcharge on premiums, and the 'reasonable alternative' that waives it is, more and more often, verified adherence to a GLP-1.

So a second market grew back. Offshore peptide vendors sold retatrutide as a research chemical for a year before the FDA approved it in March 2028, and they still undercut its $1,299 list price by a factor of ten. Some buyers want the newest molecule. Others want no record at all. Since summer, the same channels have sold unidentified 'myostatin' injectables. They are riding Lilly's filing for a muscle-sparing combination whose phase 3 cut lean-mass loss to about a tenth of weight lost. The fitness industry and the analysts talk about the skinny-frail problem in the past tense, though the FDA will not rule until 2029.

The labels grew too. Since mid-2027 every incretin label lists reduced interest or pleasure: about 1.8 percent of users against 0.8 percent on placebo, dose-related and usually reversible. Clinicians call it uncommon and ask two screening questions at each dose step. The same mechanism now has an approved use in smoking cessation for the Wegovy pill. Semaglutide also has a dementia-risk indication for people with diabetes and heart disease, approved on a seven-to-six advisory vote. That label has done more for the drug's reputation among the healthy middle-aged than its evidence supports.

In the north Dallas suburbs, among women in their forties to sixties, being on it is like having a dentist. Being off it invites a gentle question at book club. Restaurants there sell small plates and protein bowls. Plus-size racks at the mall have shrunk, and the regional chain that sold them is in restructuring. Distillers cut their forecasts again. Musicians in Austin talk openly about lowering doses before tours. Couples' counsellors ask about dose changes at intake.

Nothing has collapsed. Obesity rates edge down; food companies sell less per person at higher prices per gram; the pharmaceutical duopoly has reorganised around volume. What has hardened is a ledger. On one side are people whose coverage includes a monitor, people who pay cash privately, and people buying unlabelled vials. On the other is a growing population that has stopped, regained, and is asked to explain why.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk, fifty-one, dispatches school buses for a county district outside Toledo. At 5:40 she pinches her stomach, clicks the pen, and holds it for six seconds until the light goes green. The light means the app has the dose. The app talks to the wellness vendor. The vendor talks to the plan that dropped her weight-loss coverage in January but still waives the forty-two-dollar monthly surcharge, as long as the green lights keep coming.

The pen is the authorised generic. Sixty-nine dollars at the Kroger pharmacy, paid on the same card as the groceries.

At the depot the radio crackles. A driver named Ray, who stopped in March, asks if anyone has antacids. He has gained back the twenty pounds and tells people it's his knee. Nobody asks.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap and puts the other half back in the foil for tomorrow.

Her sister texts a photo of a vial with a handwritten label: RETA 10MG. A guy on Telegram, a hundred and twenty a vial. No app, she writes. No anybody. Denise types be careful and deletes it, then sends a heart.

After work her husband Gary is on the porch, not smoking, on his third week of the pill the doctor gave him for that. He says the cigarettes taste like pennies now.

At dinner their son asks whether she's still on it. She says yes. He nods like she has answered a question about the weather.

At night the app asks two questions. Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy? She looks at the guitar in the corner and taps No.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA approves semaglutide for dementia risk reduction in type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular disease after a 7–6 advisory vote
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the event is dated 2028-06, but the indications list says May 2028. No pivotal evidence or sNDA filing is shown, and the 2026 baseline has no dementia program, so a fast approval on a split vote is asserted rather than derived.

Mechanism: no connected semaglutide pen exists in the baseline, and the authorised generic is a standard retail pen. Four state Medicaid programs wiring pen telemetry into claims within about 14 months has no shown chain. The prose pen that turns green and reports to a wellness vendor reads as a convenient narrative device.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third and older adults who lost Bridge coverage make up most of the off-drug population.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: only ~0.8M lost Bridge coverage against ~17.7M off-drug adults, and the income split does not show the bottom third as a majority of that group. The note itself says the off-drug group skews to the middle and bottom thirds, so this claim does not reconcile with the figures.

rationale.badness: The main harms are benefit conditioning on pharmacy-claims adherence and BMI-linked wellness surcharges, which push people toward unrecorded gray-market vials. A large cycling off-drug population is asked to explain regain, and an unmeasured body-composition ratchet adds to the health ledger. Anhedonia is nameable and labelled at ~1 in 100, and gray-market harms exceed 4,000 reports, so this is a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe. Epistemic harm is moderate because the effects are measured. Autonomy and inequality score highest because privacy becomes the access barrier.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and events. Adoption is exactly −0.8 pp, the authorised generic is an event, the muscle-preserving combo is realised as a Jun 2028 filing, and anhedonia labelling, gray-market resurgence, normalisation, benefits conditioning and niche_side_effect are all present. The dementia and nicotine approval dates conflict between the indications list and the events, which costs a little. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including price to adherence conditioning to gray market, and the Bridge expiry and employer retreat. Asserted pieces are the dementia approval (claim 1), connected-pen telemetry (claim 2), the 'most of the off-drug population' line (claim 3), and indications approved only two years after 'anecdotal' evidence. magnitude: 10.2% on drug and 17% ever are inside the envelope, though ever-used is near its 17.2 ceiling. The user count, payer split (8.5+4.0+2.5+8.0+3.5=26.5M), age bands (≈10.2) and Bridge spend (1.4M×$245×12≈$4.1B) all reconcile, and the retatrutide 13-month and CagriSema approvals are allowed. Deductions: the off-drug majority claim (claim 3) and equating the one-year persistence figure with lifetime never-stopped share.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Kowalczyk day-in-the-life shows rather than explains: the green-light pen, the wellness vendor, half a turkey wrap, Ray's 'knee', the Telegram vial, Gary's pennies-tasting cigarettes and the guitar in the corner. The world fields add specific subgroups (Plano and Frisco women, musicians, recruits stopping to enlist, couples counsellors). Many scenes and characters are implied.

least_plausible_claims.quote: adjunct to smoking/vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (Wegovy pill, Jul 2028)
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the 2026 evidence for nicotine was anecdotal and observational, yet a phase 3 programme and a labelled approval are asserted within two years with no trial shown. The indication is dated Jul 2028 here but sits in the 2028-06 event, so the world contradicts itself.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Lilly reported phase 3 of bimagrumab + tirzepatide (Q1 2028): lean mass fell from ~33% of weight lost to ~9%, with similar total loss.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: bimagrumab was only in trials in 2026, and a completed phase 3 plus a June 2028 BLA is very fast. A cut in lean-mass loss to about a quarter of baseline, with no loss of total weight, is also an optimistic effect size.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage for weight management fell 60% → 42% (2028 survey).
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: an 18-point drop in two years is far steeper than the 2026 baseline, where 14% had dropped or planned to drop by 2027. The only causal link offered is that some carriers cite the $69 generic, which is thin for a drop this large.

rationale.badness: The drug is cheap and widely available, but coverage is now tied to surveillance: connected-pen logs, BMI surcharges and a 'reasonable alternative standard' defined as verified adherence. That drives autonomy to 6.5, and some users go to the unregulated gray market just to avoid records. A growing off-drug population skews to the bottom third and older adults who lost Bridge coverage, and 'are you off it?' becomes a class marker. Anhedonia is measured and labelled, which keeps epistemic and flourishing scores moderate. Overall it is a harder society with new losers rather than a refusable one.

mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as the $69 price pushing employers to drop cover and the conditioning leading to gray-market use. Weaknesses are the nicotine and dementia approvals asserted with little trial basis, the fast bimagrumab phase 3, and date inconsistencies (dementia 'May 2028' versus a 2028-06 event; smoking 'Jul 2028' versus the same June event). 
magnitude: Current use (10.2) and ever-use (17, near the 17.2 cap) are in bounds, and income and age bands bracket the national figure. The payer split sums to 26.5M, the Bridge spend arithmetic is $4.1B/yr, the CagriSema and retatrutide timing rules are respected, and the off-drug counts reconcile. The only looseness is equating the never-stopped share with the one-year persistence figure.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Kowalczyk scene is concrete: the pen light, the wellness vendor, the Kroger card, her sister's Telegram vial, Ray's 'knee', Gary's cigarettes tasting like pennies, and the guitar screening question. It implies many more scenes: couples counsellors, tour musicians, recruits stopping to enlist, Plano book clubs. least_plausible_claims.quote: they still undercut its $1,299 list price by a factor of ten
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. A $120 vial labelled 'RETA 10MG' is roughly one week at a 10 mg dose, so a month costs about $480 at high doses. That is nowhere near a tenfold undercut.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Under-18: ~0.3% of all children (~220k), up from ~0.1% in 2026.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. Paediatric use triples in two years while adult use falls, the Bridge pilot expires and coverage is being conditioned. The note offers no chain for the rise, and the 2026 baseline was only about 0.6% of children with obesity.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Lilly reported phase 3 of bimagrumab + tirzepatide (Q1 2028): lean mass fell from ~33% of weight lost to ~9%, with similar total loss.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. Bimagrumab was only 'in trials' in 2026, and the candidate moves it to a completed phase 3 and a BLA filing within about two years. The lean-mass cut is dramatic and the speed is asserted, not shown.

rationale.badness: Autonomy is the worst dimension. Coverage is conditioned on refill adherence, connected-pen dose logs and BMI-linked wellness surcharges, and some users go to the unmonitored gray market to avoid records ('conditioning_or_surveillance'). Inequality is high: the off-drug population (about 17.7M) skews to the bottom third and to older adults who lost Bridge coverage, and the gray market carries unidentified 'myostatin' injectables. The world is a recognisably harder one with new losers, but nothing collapses, anhedonia is measured and labelled at about 1 in 100, and some prices fall, so it stops short of structural horror.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is realised and traceable. Adoption is exactly -0.8 pp (11→10.2). The $69 authorised generic is an event and the only US generic. Employer coverage falls to 42%. The anhedonia label is dated Jun 2027. Dementia and nicotine indications appear. The muscle-sparing combination is realised as a filing, as the envelope allows. Gray-market resurgence and Medicaid conditioning are present, and the personality layer stays a niche side effect. mechanism: Adoption falls for stated reasons (Bridge expiry, employer retreat, conditioning, partly offset by cheap cash access), and the authorised-generic motive is shown. Several other changes are asserted: the paediatric tripling, a dementia approval on a contested vote, a smoking-cessation label with no trial path, the bimagrumab phase 3 timeline and the military recruiting rule (see claims 2 and 3). magnitude: Every population figure sits inside the envelope. Ever-used is 17 (limit 17.2), and the income and age bands average to 10.2. Payer counts sum to 26.5M. The Medicare arithmetic (1.4M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.1B; 0.6M + 0.8M = 1.4M) and the paediatric count (0.3% ≈ 220k) reconcile. Approval timing is legal: retatrutide was filed in Feb 2027 and approved Mar 2028, and the generic has an event mechanism. Minor gaps remain: current users compute to about 10.3, not 10.2, and the cash high of $1,299 sits against an unchanged $1,349 list. The gray-market price claim (claim 1) also misstates the price gap.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Kowalczyk scenes are concrete and show rather than explain: the pen light, the foil-wrapped half-wrap, Ray's 'knee', the Telegram vial text, Gary's pennies line and the two-question app. The world fields add dating-app 'on it / off it / never' profiles, 'skip weeks' around weddings, musicians dose-cutting before tours and Plano/Frisco social norms. Many implied characters and scenes are available. The prose leans slightly on summary exposition between scenes.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA approves semaglutide for dementia risk reduction in type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular disease after a 7–6 advisory vote
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the event is dated 2028-06, but the indications list says May 2028. No pivotal evidence or sNDA filing is shown, and the 2026 baseline has no dementia program, so a fast approval on a split vote is asserted rather than derived.

Mechanism: no connected semaglutide pen exists in the baseline, and the authorised generic is a standard retail pen. Four state Medicaid programs wiring pen telemetry into claims within about 14 months has no shown chain. The prose pen that turns green and reports to a wellness vendor reads as a convenient narrative device.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third and older adults who lost Bridge coverage make up most of the off-drug population.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: only ~0.8M lost Bridge coverage against ~17.7M off-drug adults, and the income split does not show the bottom third as a majority of that group. The note itself says the off-drug group skews to the middle and bottom thirds, so this claim does not reconcile with the figures.

rationale.badness: The main harms are benefit conditioning on pharmacy-claims adherence and BMI-linked wellness surcharges, which push people toward unrecorded gray-market vials. A large cycling off-drug population is asked to explain regain, and an unmeasured body-composition ratchet adds to the health ledger. Anhedonia is nameable and labelled at ~1 in 100, and gray-market harms exceed 4,000 reports, so this is a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe. Epistemic harm is moderate because the effects are measured. Autonomy and inequality score highest because privacy becomes the access barrier.
